**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, N = 14.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An element, W, (where W is not the usual symbol) exhibits isotopy. The isotopes $^{47}_{22}W$ and $^{49}_{22}W$ have relative abundances 60% and 40% respectively.

(i) What is isotopy?

(ii) What makes the two isotopes different?

(iii) Calculate the relative atomic mass of W. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Isotopy (isotopes):** atoms of the same element, with the **same atomic number (same number of protons)** but **different mass numbers** (different numbers of neutrons).

(ii) They differ in their **number of neutrons**: $47 - 22 = 25$ neutrons in $^{47}_{22}W$ and $49 - 22 = 27$ neutrons in $^{49}_{22}W$ (so they have different mass numbers).

(iii) Relative atomic mass = weighted average of the mass numbers:

$A_r = \dfrac{(47 \times 60) + (49 \times 40)}{100} = \dfrac{2820 + 1960}{100} = \dfrac{4780}{100} = \mathbf{47.8}$

questions.enonce_markdown:
Consider the reactions.

A: $\mathrm{HCl(aq)} + \mathrm{NaOH(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaCl(aq)} + \mathrm{H_2O(l)}$   $\Delta H = -57.12$ kJ/mol

B: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH(l)} + 3\mathrm{O_2(g)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO_2(g)} + 3\mathrm{H_2O(l)}$   $\Delta H = -1273$ kJ/mol

(i) Based on the reactants, identify the type of reaction represented by; A: ......... B: .........

(ii) Based on the energy changes, identify the type of enthalpy change represented by A and B.

(iii) Define enthalpy change

(iv) What volume of carbon dioxide gas will be evolved from reaction B when 5.2 g of $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$ is burnt at room temperature? *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **A:** an acid reacting with a base: a **neutralisation** reaction. **B:** a fuel (ethanol) reacting with oxygen: a **combustion** (oxidation) reaction.

(ii) For both, $\Delta H$ is negative: heat is given out to the surroundings, so both are **exothermic** reactions (A: enthalpy of neutralisation; B: enthalpy of combustion).

(iii) **Enthalpy change** is the heat energy change (heat given out or taken in) accompanying a chemical reaction at constant pressure, for the amounts of substances shown in the balanced equation (measured in kJ/mol).

(iv) Molar mass of ethanol: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH} = 2(12.0) + 6(1.0) + 16.0 = 46\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.

Moles of ethanol: $n = \dfrac{5.2}{46} = 0.113\ \mathrm{mol}$.

From the equation, 1 mol of ethanol gives 2 mol of $\mathrm{CO_2}$, so $n(\mathrm{CO_2}) = 2 \times 0.113 = 0.226\ \mathrm{mol}$.

Volume of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ (molar volume $24000\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ at room temperature): $V = 0.226 \times 24000 = 5426\ \mathrm{cm^3}$, that is about **5430 cm$^3$** ($5.43\ \mathrm{dm^3}$).
